name: City Council Special Meeting of November 27, 2019
minutes_text:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING
  OF NOVEMBER 27, 2019

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE PARKING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
WATER AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER OF SPECIAL MEETING: 6:04 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL:

  Andre Quintero, Mayor/Chair – present
  Jerry G. Velasco, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Jessica Ancona, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Quintero
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco  5-0

4.  INVOCATION: Mayor Quintero

5.  FLAG SALUTE: Mayor Quintero

6.  SPECIAL MEETING PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING AGENDIZED MATTERS ONLY:
  None

  As provided under Government Code Section 54954.3, this time has been set aside for
  persons in the audience to provide comment or make inquiries on matters appearing on
  this Special Meeting agenda only. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a meeting, persons who wish to address
  the body are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be limited to
  three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their speaking time
  to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons. All comments or queries
  presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the body as a whole and not to any
  specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any member of the body except
  through the presiding official of the meeting, members of the body are under no
  obligation to respond to questions posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying
  responses to any comment made or questions posed. The body may not engage in any
  sort of prolonged discussion or deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on
  matters that are not listed on this Special Meeting agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police of the City of El Monte, or such member,
  or members of the Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve
  as the Sergeant-at-Arms of the meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders
  and instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the body or its members, members of
  the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to policies barring harassment based upon a person’s race, religious creed,
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of November 27, 2019

  color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition, marital status,
  gender, sexual orientation or age.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

  7.1  A Public Hearing to Consider and Approve an Ordinance of the City of El Monte,
  California Adopting the Commercial Cannabis Regulation and Public Safety Initiative
  Measure Without Alteration Pursuant to California Elections Code Section 9215(a).

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1.  Open the public hearing;
  2.  Receive the presentation from staff;
  3.  Pose questions to staff;
  4.  Allow members of the public to offer comment;
  5.  Pose follow up questions to staff;
  6.  Close the public hearing;
  7.  Approve the attached Ordinance for first reading by majority vote pursuant to
  California Elections Code Section 9215(a).

  Total Cost: N/A  Account No: N/A
  Is the cost of this item budgeted? N/A

  Ordinance No. 2960

m) Mayor Quintero
s) Councilmember Morales
Open Public Hearing
5-0

Kewei Zhao – I want to voice my opposition to the approval and one particular reason is that the
petitioners purposely mislead the public by saying it is for the safety of the neighborhood. I want
you guys to vote no for the petition.

Ron Williams – Here we are again we are in violation of the Brown Act which is a criminal
offense. I hope to see you all in prison for those of you who vote yes on this. We know the
legality of marijuana can be overturned. We say no and you don’t listen.

Irene Chan – I have a question this initiative has only 10 percent of the voter signatures and
there were over 10 percent of voter signatures who opposed this. If the City does not put this
on the ballot for voters to vote on and you just make the decision between 5 of you is hard not to
question if there isn’t a personal benefit.

Fenglan Liu – I respectfully have some gifts from El Monte voters. This is for the Mayor and
Mayor Pro Tem you are being served that you are being recalled. Today’s meeting is illegal you
violated the Brown Act. People have 72 hours to get noticed you have special meeting. Special
Meeting is for an emergency situation. Anybody who votes today is illegal this meeting is illegal.

Ken Meng – Our Country is based on religion we trust God and we believe in God and that is
why the Mayor had a prayer before we started the meeting. Prayer is not just for prayer it is to
get help from God and the commandment tell us to help people instead of harming people.

Gary Johnston – I have been a resident for over 60 years I think that this is wrong. I have not
been happy since the whole situation started it seems as though everything was done in back
corners. No one seems to know when things are done until they are done like tonight. I think we
have responsibility not for ourselves but for our children. This is not going to be healthy and it is
not going to stop illegal drugs.

Gabriel Ramirez – Is it 24 hours or 72 hours. Is this a special meeting or a regular meeting?
We will see tonight who are putting the interest of the people first instead of the marijuana big
donations.

Sam Meng – I Oppose this because of the simple fact of the implications of legalization and
what it includes as normalization. This will impact our future and how they think of marijuana.

  2
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of November 27, 2019

As you know the FDA there is research going on. We do not need legalized marijuana we do
not need this kind this is sending a wrong message to our children.

Alice Leung – I would like to request respectfully that the City Council think about that this will
be very harmful for the Country. This will be very harmful for the children of this Country.

Andy Huang – I am here to support the initiative. What I wanted to present are medical facts. I
brought here over 1,000 medical studies there is currently a lack of clean medicinal product to
save our community. I represent hundreds of patients. Marijuana is a gateway to health.

Maureen Wan – I haven’t prepared well because I received short notice of this meeting. I am
asking that you do not approve this Ordinance. I wonder why we are so rushed to approve this
Ordinance. Why don’t we put this on the ballot to let the voters make a decision?

Jason Witt – I am a police officer for the Los Angeles Police Department. I am a certified drug
recognition expert I am trained in stopping people for DUI. In my City we have over 10,000
officers our DUIs due to marijuana have gone over 300 percent since the laws have changed.
The dispensaries in my City have been robbed constantly.

Theresa Sainz – I don’t want marijuana here in El Monte. I have 4 children, I have lived here
since 1996 and right now it is difficult. We do not want marijuana in El Monte it is not good.

Zig Jiang – I am going to repeat the Brown Act. This meeting is very special, yes it is very
special. When and where did you post it? City Councilmembers should vote no on this.

Diane Cheung – I am very grateful that I have an opportunity to speak today. I have been a
teacher almost all my life. Medical doctors have said that marijuana is very bad for a
development brain and it is not healthy for people. We support medical use but not recreational
use and you already know that.

Michelle Wu – Tonight I urge you not to approve the Ordinance. I just want to ask what the
urgent need to hold a special meeting?

Tom Hung – I am here to support the initiative.

Terrance Vuong – I just want to say that I support medical marijuana I think this is going to be
good for the City and it is going to be good for the people.
Damien Martin – I represent Green Jobs for the people it is one of the political action
committees supporting these measures. I am here to support the initiative.

m) Mayor Quintero
s) Mayor Pro Tem Velasco
Close Public Hearing
5-0

m) Mayor Quintero
s) Councilmember Morales  3-2 (Councilmembers Ancona and Martinez Muela No)
First Reading of Ordinance No. 2960

Break at 7:50 pm
Return at 7:57 pm

8.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  8A.  Mayor Quintero

  8A.1  Discussion Regarding a $25,000 Sponsorship to the El Monte Promise
  Foundation (Tamalada).

  Gabriel Ramirez – I inow this item we are talking about and I was looking and I
  know our tax dollars have been donated before $5,000 and now you want
  $25,000 to a non-profit organization. Can we ask our City Attorney if this is legal
  because you and Mayor Pro Tem are active member of this particular
  organization? If we are going to vote on this I suggest that both the Mayor and
  Mayor Pro Tem recuse themselves since they are members.

  3
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of November 27, 2019

  Irma Zamorano – I also have a concerned with these $25,000 being donated to
  the El Monte Promise because it is a conflict of interest because Mayor Pro Tem
  Velasco and Councilmember Morales you are active members of these. I would
  like to see an audit to see what the money is being used. We have never
  received any information regarding this.

  Councilmember Morales – If I can make one additional comment I want to make
  sure for the record that I mention that not only do we have an MOU in supporting
  a non-profit who is very much involved and has many community partners
  including our school districts including Rio Hondo College. In addition, the White
  House and the previous Administration have highlighted all of the great work that
  this organization is doing for the community and our children.

  Councilmember Ancona – Over the years I think since the El Monte Promise was
  established and the Tamalada began I have attended almost yearly I am a big
  supporter of this program. However, I wouldn’t say I am comfortable approving
  $25,000 of tax payer money to this program considering that in the past we
  donated $2,500 last year, 2017 - $2,500, 2016 - $2,500. So to increase it by
  1,000 percent seems rather like a lot of money especially when we have cut back
  on some of our programs. I personally donated to this organization, the Anconas
  have donated. Since we barely balanced the budget I think we should continue
  to watch our pennies it seems like a huge increase even in looking at the
  sponsorship levels.

  Mayor Quintero – If I may make my motion to move to approve the $25,000
  event sponsorship allocation we are going to have a separate sponsorship
  designation this time around they are going to be launching a kindergarten
  imitative and we would like to be sponsors of that. I know that the City of San
  Francisco and other cities have their promises with their children and this is our
  opportunity to get attention on these types of accounts to help families save for
  college and we want to be on the forefront.

  Mayor Pro Tem Velasco – As you know I am very supportive of non-profit
  organizations because that is where I come from and there was some mention
  regarding helping our Police Department. I think that this program is basically to
  help the Police Department because we want to get the kids before they go in the
  wrong direction and this is the way to go and it is to help the non-profit, help the
  children, help education, help them go to school, help them go to college, help
  them learn how to save.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – I wanted to make sure that this is not
  considered a gift of public funds. Typically in the past if we have done a
  sponsorship it is typically a sponsorship for a table for this event. And this
  particular sponsorship goes above and beyond the table cost so Mr. City
  Attorney how is this not considered a gift of public fund? So, the question is what
  was the reported surplus for this particular this year. I just wanted to make sure
  that we are very clear that we are going and dipping into money that is not
  budgeted. Before I continue I want to make it clear that I am a fan of the El
  Monte Promise. But I also wanted to make it clear that I am also a fan of the
  Veterans in our City, could you use $25,000 I am sure you can. I am fan of the
  Hope House and Byron Thompson School could they use $25,000 yes they
  could. I am a fan of La Historia and the Historical Society could they use
  $25,000 yes they could. I am a fan of other organizations that raise money
  selling fireworks not relying on taxpayers’ money. We don’t have the money if
  we want to fundraise we can count on certain developers, people who do
  business in the City, people who want to do business in the City. We all have
  things that we care about and we all have ideas and charities within this
  community that we care about but we are not coming to the table asking for the
  taxpayer’s money to go to a specific organization. The City cannot invest in
  organizations at the $25,000 level and with all the great work that the El Monte
  Promise Foundation does I am really sorry that I cannot support this today but I
  will continue to support them individually.

m) Mayor Quintero
s) Councilmember Morales  3-2 (Councilmembers Ancona and
  Martinez Muela No)

  4
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of November 27, 2019

  Mayor Quintero – So I don’t know if this takes a formal motion and if it does we
  can put in on a subsequent meeting I know that to move money from certain
  accounts to others we may have to take certain actions. It is my understanding
  that we have about $100,000 in our community promotions account and that
  $25,000 can equally come out of that account. What we are promoting is
  education, what we are promoting is higher education and economic
  development activity because we are investing in the young people of our
  community. When someone says that we cannot afford to invest our children I
  can tell you from my perspective we can. I want to give special thanks to staff,
  you guys have really had to endure so much. When I see you again it will be after
  celebrating 10 years in office. On December 1st I stood over there by that podium
  with my daughter in hand and I swore in as Mayor of the City. I never imagined
  that I would be the Mayor of this City but you never know how life is going to
  guide you or direct you in what direction and I certainly never thought I would be
  the longest serving Mayor in this City’s history. I am honored to be able to
  represent the community that I live in and have lived in since I was 6 years old. I
  want to give a special thanks to the staff, the staff that we’ve had throughout the
  years what they have had to do over the years has been extraordinary.

8B.  Mayor Pro Tem Velasco

  I also want to congratulate the El Monte Lions and the Cross-Country Teams I
  know that I recommended to the City Manager that maybe there is something
  that we can do whether it is a small parade and that we can do it during the
  Holiday House to conserve funds. This could be a joint venture with the school
  districts.

8C.  Councilwoman Ancona

  I want to echo the sentiments of congratulating our El Monte Lions 13-0 is
  outstanding really proud to bring home another CIF Championship here in the
  City of El Monte a couple of years ago was Arroyo. Just want to wish everyone a
  Happy Thanksgiving be safe out there and enjoy your families.

8D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  This past weekend we had the El Monte Lions bring home a CIF Championship.
  Congratulations Lions it is a big deal. I look forward to celebrating with our Lions
  here at the next regularly scheduled meeting potentially. They went undefeated
  this season 13-0. This could be a really hard seat to sit in we try to find the right
  words to not hurt feelings and sometimes we make mistakes. We try to continue
  to live out the role that we are supposed to and sometimes we make mistakes
  and I just want to be clear today and thankful that we are humans and that we
  make mistakes and that we cherish humanity those who are blessed to be in
  your circle friends and family I am grateful for you. City staff I am grateful. For
  this time and this seat to be your Councilwoman I am grateful and like I said it is
  not easy all the time but I will take it on any day because it has been a dream of
  a lifetime to continue to serve you. On behalf of myself and my family we wish
  you a Happy Thanksgiving.

8E.  Councilwoman Morales

  I too agree that we are very happy that our El Monte Lions have made it through
  their football season and they do need the recognition but they also need our
  financial support to make sure that they are seen through college so that they
  know we are keeping them in line so that if they get to a community college if that
  is what they want to do, so that they get to a UC if that is what they want to do, a
  Cal State U if that is what they want to do. So we will bring them in and we will
  recognize them but we also have to bring and recognize the cross-country team
  for Arroyo High School both the boys and girls they made it to CIS State
  Championship. I also wanted to mention thank you staff for putting up our shop
  local given that we will have out Black Friday. So statistics show that for every
  $100 dollars that your purchase in a particular community $67 stay in that
  community and so remember to do your purchases locally. Again, thank you to

  5
   City Council Special Meeting Minutes of November 27, 2019

  staff for all the work that you do. Thank you for spending countless hours in your
  office to make sure that the work of the City is done you are very selfless with
  your time knowing that you have a family at home. Happy Thanksgiving.

9.  ADJOURNMENT:

  The next Regular Meeting of the City Council will be held on December 3, 2019 at 6:00
  p.m. This Agenda will be posted on the City’s website, www.ci.el-monte.ca.us, and
  physically posted no less than 72 hours prior to the start of the subject regular meeting.
  Although it is the City’s practice and desire to electronically post a copy of this Agenda
  along with supporting material as part of its website posting, the size or formatting of
  certain supporting materials may render their website posting infeasible. Nevertheless,
  all supporting materials related to any item on this Agenda, that is made available to the
  members of the council may be inspected by members of the public at the City Clerk’s
  Office located at 11333 Valley Boulevard, El Monte, Monday through Thursday, 7:00 am
  – 5:30 pm. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at 626-580-2016.

  All public meetings and events sponsored or conducted by the City of El Monte are held
  in sites accessible to persons with disabilities. Requests for accommodations may be
  made by calling the office of the City Clerk at (626) 580-2016 at least three (3) working
  days prior to the event, if possible. This Agenda and copies of documents distributed at
  the meeting are available in alternative formats upon request.

  _____________________________
  Catherine A. Eredia, City Clerk
  City of El Monte

APPROVED:

_________________________________
Andre Quintero, Mayor
City of El Monte
